title: Source, Myth, or Contested?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Classify ten statements about Byzantine Constantinople as a primary source, a myth, contested history or settled history, with the reason shown after each answer.

learningObjectives: Classify ten statements about Byzantine Constantinople as a primary source, a myth, contested history or settled history, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.

keyQuestions: What kind of statement is this?
Who wrote it, for whom, and why?
When does this story first appear?
Who is this past important to now?
commonMisconceptions: A primary source is a true source.
A myth is a lie and has no value.
Any disagreement means the facts are unknown, when in contested history the facts are agreed and the meaning is disputed.
A story told by every tour guide must be history.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on ten statements (mastery: 8 of 10).
Explain why the eyewitness accounts of Procopius and Choniates are primary sources even though each is one-sided.
Classify a new story heard on site, such as the weeping column, and say how to test it.
